causal:influence:adipose_tissue_mass:neg.evidence: do(increase adipose mass)/high-fat-diet perturbation lowers hepatic 25-hydroxylase activity and serum 25(OH)D. causal:influence:adipose_tissue_mass:neg.mechanism: Increased adiposity/obesity downregulates hepatic CYP2R1 (the principal vitamin D 25-hydroxylase), reducing conversion of cholecalciferol (D3) to 25-hydroxyvitamin D. Within-scale ORGAN_SYSTEM -> ORGAN_SYSTEM; analyte is a downstream sink, so no new path is created through the homeostatic feedback core.

causal:influence:airway_resistance:negat.evidence: West JB Respiratory Physiology 9e Ch 1 — VA = minute ventilation − dead-space ventilation; resistance reduces effective flow at given driving pressure; GINA 2023 Guidelines — bronchospasm in asthma raises airway resistance, reduces FEV1/VA; Miller MR et al 2005 Eur Respir J 26:319 — spirometric measures of airway resistance inversely correlate with alveolar ventilation; pharmacological bronchodilators (salbutamol, do(airway_resistance -)) restore VA in obstructive disease. | intervention: do(airway_resistance +) — inhaled methacholine challenge or allergen bronchoprovocation raises airway resistance, reducing alveolar ventilation; do(airway_resistance -) — salbutamol/ipratropium bronchodilation reduces airway resistance, restoring alveolar ventilation.
causal:influence:airway_resistance:negat.mechanism: Airway resistance (R) and alveolar ventilation (VA) are linked by the fundamental respiratory equation: VA = ΔP / R (for laminar flow), where ΔP is the driving pressure generated by respiratory muscles. When airway resistance rises (bronchospasm, mucus plugging, bronchiole smooth-muscle contraction), the same muscular effort produces less airflow per unit time, reducing effective alveolar ventilation. In asthma, bronchoconstriction raises airway resistance and reduces VA, causing hypercapnia and hypoxaemia.

This lysosomal storage drives microglial and macrophage activation in the CNS and peripheral tissues, similar to other glycoprotein storage disorders. Reduced alpha-L-fucosidase activity (LoF) leads to accumulation of fucosylated substrates -> macrophage lysosomal dysfunction -> macrophage activation. Sign is negative: lower enzyme activity -> higher macrophage activation.

The causal direction is confirmed by carbonic anhydrase inhibitors that reduce CSF production and lower ICP in idiopathic intracranial hypertension.

[citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:il1beta:positive:plasma.mechanism: IL-1 beta is a major cytokine inducer of hepatic serum amyloid A acute-phase synthesis; raising circulating IL-1 beta increases hepatocyte SAA transcription/synthesis and thus plasma SAA.

[citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:il6_stat3_signaling:pos.mechanism: IL-6 binds IL6R/gp130, activating JAK1; phospho-STAT3 dimerizes and binds the STAT3 element of the HAMP promoter (disposition -> transcriptional activation process), raising hepcidin mRNA synthesis rate (basis of anemia of inflammation).

causal:influence:intestinal_b12_absorpti.evidence: Guyton & Hall, Medical Physiology, 11th ed. Ch.32 (Red Blood Cells, Anemia, and Polycythemia) §Maturation Failure Caused by Poor Absorption of Vitamin B12 from the Gastrointestinal Tract—Pernicious Anemia: “vitamin B12 is transported into the blood during the next few hours by the process of pinocytosis”
causal:influence:intestinal_b12_absorpti.mechanism: absorbed B12 is transported into blood and stored/released, setting the plasma cobalamin pool

[citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:intracellular_adp:posit.mechanism: ADP is the phosphoryl-acceptor substrate of mitochondrial ATP synthase (complex V); increased ADP availability raises ATP synthesis flux

causal:influence:isovaleryl_coa_dehydrog.mechanism: hydrolysis of accumulated isovaleryl-CoA yields free isovaleric acid; reduced IVD activity raises plasma isovaleric acid

causal:influence:klotho_activity:negativ.evidence: Nakatani et al., FASEB J 2009, PMID 18835926, DOI 10.1096/fj.08-114397: klotho-null mice had increased renal NaPi2a and hyperphosphatemia, and recombinant FGF23 lowered phosphate in wild-type and Fgf23-null mice but not in klotho-null or double-null mice.

causal:influence:kynu_activity:negative:.evidence: KYNU deficiency / hydroxykynureninuria (OMIM 236800 / VCRL2); PMC2019216 — 'Hydroxykynureninuria: a case of Abnormal Tryptophan Metabolism Probably Due to a Deficiency of Kynureninase'; OMIM 605197 — 'kynureninase deficiency; 3-hydroxykynurenine elevated in urine organic acids in KYNU-mutant patients'; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (kynurenine pathway: KYNU converts 3-hydroxykynurenine → 3-hydroxyanthranilate). | intervention: do(KYNU activity ↓) = kynureninase deficiency / hydroxykynureninuria (OMIM 236800)
causal:influence:kynu_activity:negative:.mechanism: Kynureninase (KYNU) is a pyridoxal-5-phosphate-dependent enzyme that cleaves 3-hydroxykynurenine to 3-hydroxyanthranilate + alanine (and separately cleaves kynurenine to anthranilate + alanine). With KYNU deficiency, 3-hydroxykynurenine cannot be converted and accumulates (∂[3-HK]/∂(KYNU activity) < 0). KYNU mutations also cause vertebral, cardiac, renal, and limb defects syndrome-2 (VCRL2).

causal:influence:kynureninase_activity:n.evidence: Fukuoka S et al. 2007, J Inherit Metab Dis 30:184-188 (PMID 17334708) — xanthurenic aciduria due to KYNU mutation; OMIM 236800 hydroxykynureninuria — elevated kynurenine, 3-hydroxykynurenine, xanthurenate; Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry, kynurenine pathway. | intervention: KYNU LoF (hydroxykynureninuria / xanthurenic aciduria): kynureninase activity DOWN → 3-hydroxykynurenine → xanthurenate via KAT, urinary xanthurenate UP [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:kynureninase_activity:n.mechanism: Kynureninase (KYNU) hydrolyzes 3-hydroxykynurenine → 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid + L-alanine. KYNU LoF causes 3-hydroxykynurenine to accumulate; it is then transaminated by kynurenine aminotransferases (KAT, PLP-dependent) to xanthurenic acid, which is excreted in urine. Elevated xanthurenate is diagnostic of KYNU deficiency (xanthurenic aciduria, hydroxykynureninuria).

causal:influence:lcat_activity:negative:.evidence: Glomset JA. J Lipid Res. 1968;9:155-167; OMIM 245900; Barter P, Rye KA. HDL subfractions and LCAT reaction. Curr Opin Lipidol. 2006 | intervention: LCAT loss-of-function (OMIM 245900): do(LCAT activity down) -> HDL3 subfractions up (HDL3 accumulates as HDL2 falls)
causal:influence:lcat_activity:negative:.mechanism: LCAT converts HDL3 (small, cholesterol-poor, pre-beta HDL) to HDL2 (large, alpha-HDL) by esterifying surface free cholesterol; more LCAT activity depletes the HDL3 precursor pool by driving it to HDL2; LCAT deficiency causes HDL3 accumulation relative to HDL2.

causal:influence:leptin:negative:plasma_.evidence: "Direct central nervous system infusion of leptin increases glucose disposal and rapidly normalizes blood glucose in Lepob/ob mice" Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 39, p 1561
causal:influence:leptin:negative:plasma_.mechanism: central leptin action increases glucose disposal and normalizes blood glucose via hypothalamic circuits

causal:influence:leptin:positive:gnrh.evidence: Administration of recombinant leptin to hypogonadal ob/ob mice and to rats experiencing pubertal delay associated with food restriction in the rat partially reverses the hypogonadism. Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 26
causal:influence:leptin:positive:gnrh.mechanism: leptin acts on ventral premammillary neurons to stimulate glutamate release which activates GnRH neurons; leptin-deficient ob/ob mice have hypogonadotropic hypogonadism reversed by leptin administration

causal:influence:leptin:positive:lepr_si.evidence: "Leptin then circulates to the brain, where it moves across the blood-brain barrier by facilitated diffusion and occupies leptin receptors at multiple sites in the hypothalamus, especially the POMC neurons of the arcuate nuclei." — Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, Ch. 71, p. 868
causal:influence:leptin:positive:lepr_si.mechanism: leptin binds LEPR on arcuate POMC/AGRP neurons -> LEPR signalling activation

causal:influence:lymph_drainage_rate:neg.evidence: "Third, the increasing interstitial fluid pressure greatly increases the rate of lymph flow...This in turn carries away the excess interstitial fluid volume and excess protein that has accumulated in the spaces" — Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, ch w05
causal:influence:lymph_drainage_rate:neg.mechanism: lymphatic drainage removes protein from interstitium; increased lymph flow lowers interstitial protein concentration toward steady state

causal:influence:malonyl_coa_decarboxyla.evidence: Scriver's OMMBID / Saudubray — malonic aciduria (MLYCD, OMIM 248360)
causal:influence:malonyl_coa_decarboxyla.mechanism: malonyl-CoA decarboxylase converts malonyl-CoA to acetyl-CoA; deficiency accumulates malonyl-CoA hydrolysed to malonic acid (malonic aciduria) — reduced activity raises urinary malonate

causal:influence:mcad_activity:negative:.evidence: PMC6091831 (MCAD deficiency, OMIM 201450; C10:1 decenoylcarnitine significantly elevated, one of four primary biomarkers); GeneReviews NBK1424 (C10:1 part of MCAD deficiency acylcarnitine profile) | intervention: ACADM LoF (MCAD deficiency, OMIM 201450)
causal:influence:mcad_activity:negative:.mechanism: MCAD acts on cis-4-decenoyl-CoA and related C10:1 unsaturated medium-chain species; LoF causes decenoyl-CoA (C10:1) accumulation, with decenoylcarnitine (C10:1) elevated in MCAD deficiency — listed as one of the four primary NBS biomarkers alongside C6, C8, C10

causal:influence:mcc_activity:positive:p.evidence: OMIM 210200 (3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase 1 deficiency, MCC1D; clinical features include acute hypoglycemia, metabolic acidosis, secondary carnitine deficiency); MedlinePlus Genetics / JCI PMC199271 (MCC deficiency: very low plasma free carnitine due to 3-hydroxyisovaleryl-carnitine conjugation; very low plasma glucose is a presenting feature); Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry (leucine catabolism: 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA -> HMG-CoA -> acetyl-CoA + acetoacetate; carnitine-dependent FAO supports gluconeogenic substrates and ketogenesis during fasting). | intervention: MCC biallelic loss-of-function (MCC1D, OMIM 210200): do(MCC activity DOWN) -> leucine catabolism blocked -> 3-methylcrotonyl-carnitine accumulates -> carnitine deficiency -> impaired FAO -> fasting hypoglycemia -> plasma glucose DOWN | intervention: MCC biallelic loss-of-function (3-MCC deficiency, OMIM 210200)
causal:influence:mcc_activity:positive:p.mechanism: 3-Methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase (MCC) catalyzes the fourth step of leucine catabolism (3-methylcrotonyl-CoA -> 3-methylglutaconyl-CoA). MCC deficiency causes 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA to accumulate and conjugate with carnitine, depleting the free carnitine pool; secondary carnitine deficiency impairs mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation, removing the principal fasting fuel source and producing hypoketotic hypoglycaemia. More MCC activity preserves carnitine homeostasis, supports FAO during fasting, and maintains plasma glucose.

causal:influence:membrane_pip2_vsmc:posi.evidence: Alberts et al., Molecular Biology of the Cell, 6th ed.; (Chapter 15, Signaling through GPCRs / the inositol phospholipid pathway); “Phospholipase C cleaves PI(4,5)P2 to generate two second messengers, inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate (IP3) and diacylglycerol; IP3 releases Ca2+ from the endoplasmic reticulum.” | do(increase membrane PIP2) increases cytosolic Ca2+ (+): PIP2 is the substrate whose PLC-generated IP3 releases ER Ca2+
causal:influence:membrane_pip2_vsmc:posi.mechanism: PLC hydrolyzes membrane PIP2 to IP3; IP3 binds the ER IP3 receptor and releases stored Ca2+ into the cytosol, so available PIP2 substrate sets IP3-driven cytosolic Ca2+ rise

causal:influence:methylcrotonyl_coa_carb.evidence: PMID 29767664; (Abstract; Biochemical and molecular characterization of 3-Methylcrotonylglycinuria (PMC6082241)); “Its deficiency leads to accumulation in blood and/or urine of 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA metabolites, primarily 3-hydroxyisovaleryl-carnitine (C5-OH) in plasma and 3-methylcrotonyl-glycine (3-MCG) and 3-hydroxyisovaleric acid (3-HIVA) in urine” | MCC deficiency elevates plasma C5-OH (and urinary 3-MCG), so do(MCC down) raises C5-OH: enzyme activity --(-)--> 3-hydroxyisovalerylcarnitine. [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:methylcrotonyl_coa_carb.mechanism: 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase activity (disposition) carboxylates 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA in leucine catabolism; loss of activity backs up 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA into alternative products, primarily 3-hydroxyisovalerylcarnitine (C5-OH). MCC LoF is a natural do(low MCC) that raises C5-OH.

causal:influence:methylglutaconyl_coa_hy.evidence: Scriver's OMMBID — 3-methylglutaconic aciduria type I (AUH, OMIM 250950)
causal:influence:methylglutaconyl_coa_hy.mechanism: blocked 3-methylglutaconyl-CoA is diverted to 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutarate; reduced AUH activity raises urinary 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutarate

causal:influence:mttp_activity:positive:.evidence: Sharp D et al. Nature 1993 (MTTP mutations cause abetalipoproteinemia); OMIM 200100 (abetalipoproteinemia); Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism | intervention: MTTP loss-of-function (abetalipoproteinemia, OMIM 200100): do(MTTP activity down) -> plasma apoB-100 absent/severely reduced

causal:influence:mttp_activity:positive:.evidence: Abetalipoproteinaemia (microsomal triglyceride transfer protein deficiency), OMIM:200100 — LoF causes near-absent plasma triglycerides
causal:influence:mttp_activity:positive:.mechanism: RHEA:39011 (EC 2.3.1.51 / lipid transfer): a triacyl-sn-glycerol(in ER lumen) = a triacyl-sn-glycerol(in nascent VLDL/chylomicron); triglyceride is transferred into apoB-containing lipoprotein particles for plasma secretion; the plasma lipoprotein-bound TG is the product

causal:influence:neuraminidase_activity:.evidence: Sialidosis OMIM 256550 (NEU1 LoF); Genes 2025 PMC11855786 (sialidosis: multi-organ storage including kidney; renal involvement documented). Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, Lysosomal Storage Diseases (renal storage in oligosaccharidoses). Saudubray 'Inborn Metabolic Diseases' (sialidosis: renal involvement with proteinuria reported in severe forms). | intervention: NEU1 (neuraminidase-1) loss-of-function (sialidosis, OMIM 256550) | intervention: NEU1 loss-of-function (sialidosis, OMIM 256550)
causal:influence:neuraminidase_activity:.mechanism: Lysosomal neuraminidase-1 (NEU1) deficiency (sialidosis, OMIM 256550) causes accumulation of sialylated oligosaccharides and glycoproteins in multiple tissues including kidney podocytes and mesangial cells. Progressive lysosomal storage in glomerular cells leads to podocyte injury, proteinuria, and impaired glomerular filtration. do(NEU1 LoF) → sialic-acid-containing oligosaccharide storage in kidney → glomerular damage → GFR falls.

causal:influence:nkcc2_activity:negative.evidence: Bartter syndrome type 1 (OMIM 601678): biallelic SLC12A1 LoF mutations abolish NKCC2-mediated Cl reabsorption in the TAL, causing urinary salt (NaCl) wasting and polyuria. Boron & Boulpaep, Medical Physiology (TAL NaCl reabsorption; NKCC2). PMID 12761241 (Karolyi et al.): all Bartter type I SLC12A1 mutations result in nonfunctional NKCC2 transporters. | intervention: do(NKCC2 activity DOWN) — Bartter syndrome type 1, SLC12A1 biallelic LoF [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:nkcc2_activity:negative.mechanism: NKCC2 in the thick ascending limb apically cotransports Na-K-2Cl from the filtrate into tubular cells, reabsorbing Cl from the lumen; higher NKCC2 activity increases tubular Cl reabsorption, reducing urinary Cl excretion. Loss-of-function mutations cause Bartter syndrome type 1 (salt-wasting hypercalciuria with urinary Cl loss).

causal:influence:norepinephrine:positive.evidence: Boron & Boulpaep — beta-1 chronotropy; Guyton & Hall — sympathetic cardiac stimulation | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-081 (15.3: Autonomic Reflexes and Homeostasis): norepinephrine binds adrenergic receptors on SA-node cells, causing faster depolarization and increased heart rate.; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-094 (17.7: The Adrenal Glands): 'These hormones increase the heart rate, pulse, and blood pressure.'; OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-109 (19.5: Cardiac Physiology): 'NE shortens the repolarization period, thus speeding the rate of depolarization and contraction, which results in an increase in HR.'; OpenStax Biology 2e §bio-35.4 (35.4: The Peripheral Nervous System): 'The physiological effects of this norepinephrine release include...increasing heart rate'.
causal:influence:norepinephrine:positive.mechanism: norepinephrine at SA-node beta-1 adrenoceptors increases pacemaker If/Ca current, raising the rate of spontaneous depolarisation (positive chronotropy).

causal:influence:norepinephrine:positive.evidence: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-080 (15.2: Divisions of the Autonomic Nervous System): 'The pupils dilate when the sympathetic system is activated.' Boron & Boulpaep Medical Physiology Ch. 14 (autonomic control of the eye). Horner syndrome (sympathetic interruption, do(NE=0)): miosis, ptosis, anhidrosis — confirms NE as pupil dilator drive. Topical phenylephrine (alpha-1 agonist, do(NE-equivalent=high)) → mydriasis. | intervention: pharmacological: topical phenylephrine (alpha-1 agonist, mimics NE) → pupil dilation (mydriasis); Horner syndrome (sympathetic chain lesion, do(NE=0)) → persistent miosis; norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors raise synaptic NE and cause mild mydriasis
causal:influence:norepinephrine:positive.mechanism: Sympathetic norepinephrine activates alpha-1 adrenoceptors on the dilator pupillae muscle of the iris, causing smooth-muscle contraction and pupil dilation (mydriasis). This is the sympathetic effector limb of pupillary control; bilateral sympathetic denervation (Horner syndrome) causes miosis (pupil constriction) due to loss of this dilator drive.

causal:influence:nuclear_srebp2_activity.evidence: "SREBP2 is most important for LDL receptor transcription; its NH2-terminus contains a leucine zipper–type transcription factor structure that binds to a sterol regulatory element in the promoter of the LDL receptor gene." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 41, p. 1594
causal:influence:nuclear_srebp2_activity.mechanism: Active nuclear SREBP-2 binds sterol regulatory element in LDL receptor gene promoter → increased LDL receptor transcription → more surface LDL receptors

causal:influence:ocrl1_activity:positive.evidence: PMID 18480301; (Abstract); “Patients with Lowe syndrome do not have renal Fanconi syndrome but a selective proximal tubulopathy, variable in extent and dominated by low molecular weight proteinuria and hypercalciuria.” | Loss of OCRL activity produces hypercalciuria (decreased tubular calcium reabsorption), so OCRL activity increases renal calcium reabsorption (do(OCRL activity)->renal_calcium_reabsorption, sign +). causal:influence:osteoclast_activity:pos.evidence: PMID 23277718; (Abstract); “Reduction in bone loss during antiresorptive treatment is demonstrated by decreased excretion of hydroxyproline post antiresorptive therapy.” | do(decrease osteoclast/bone resorption, via antiresorptive drug) decreases hydroxyproline; hence higher resorption raises hydroxyproline (+) [citations PubMed-verified]
causal:influence:osteoclast_activity:pos.mechanism: osteoclastic resorption proteolyzes bone type-I collagen, liberating hydroxyproline; antiresorptive drugs that lower resorption lower hydroxyproline output

causal:influence:p5c_dehydrogenase_activ.evidence: OMMBID hyperprolinemia type II (P5C dehydrogenase / ALDH4A1 deficiency) — elevated P5C and proline
causal:influence:p5c_dehydrogenase_activ.mechanism: P5C dehydrogenase (ALDH4A1) oxidizes pyrroline-5-carboxylate -> glutamate; reduced activity (hyperprolinemia type II) causes P5C and proline to accumulate

causal:influence:pah_enzyme_activity:pos.evidence: Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry Ch. 18 (tyrosine is the PAH product; becomes dietarily essential in PKU); PKU OMIM 261600 | textbook corroboration: OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology 2e §anp-141 (24.5: Protein Metabolism): 'People afflicted with PKU lack sufficient activity of the enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase and are therefore unable to break down phenylalanine into tyrosine adequately' — PAH converts Phe to Tyr, so reduced PAH lowers plasma tyrosine; Wong, Cells: Molecules and Mechanisms §wong-6.7 (Amino Acid Synthesis - Undeclared): 'phenylalanine oxygenase reduces phenylalanine to produce the tyrosine' (tyrosine is the product)

causal:influence:pcsk9_concentration:neg.evidence: "PCSK9 is a secreted protease that promotes the degradation of the LDL receptor by interacting with the receptor so that it is targeted to the lysosome ... causal:influence:phosphoglycerate_mutase.evidence: GSD X / phosphoglycerate mutase deficiency OMIM 261670; MedlinePlus Genetics 'phosphoglycerate mutase deficiency' (exercise-induced myoglobinuria, elevated CK between episodes); PubMed 27612597 (GSD X caused by novel PGAM2 variant, elevated serum CK); Harrison's 'Metabolic Myopathies'. | intervention: do(phosphoglycerate_mutase_activity ↓) — GSD X, PGAM2 loss-of-function (autosomal recessive) [citations PubMed-verified]

causal:influence:pka_activity:positive:a.evidence: "This process cannot occur unless perilipin 1, a protein that coats small lipid droplets, is phosphorylated by protein kinase A." Williams Textbook of Endocrinology, 14th ed., ch 41, p. 1585

causal:influence:plasma_alpha1_antitryps.evidence: Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (Rodwell et al.), 31st ed.; (Chapter on Plasma Proteins / Protease inhibitors (alpha-1-antitrypsin)); “The first identified role for alpha-1 antitrypsin was to control the activity of the digestive enzyme trypsin.” | A1AT is the serpin that inhibits trypsin, so raising plasma A1AT lowers trypsin catalytic activity (do(A1AT up) -> trypsin activity down).

causal:influence:plasma_beta_hcg:positiv.mechanism: hCG binds the shared LH/hCG receptor (LHCGR) on fetal Leydig cells, stimulating StAR-mediated cholesterol transfer and the steroidogenic cascade to produce testosterone; loss-of-function LHCGR mutations abolish hCG responsiveness causing Leydig cell hypoplasia and low testosterone

causal:influence:plasma_bile_acids:posit.mechanism: Bile acids (CDCA, DCA, LCA) are the endogenous agonists of the nuclear receptor FXR (NR1H4); raising plasma / enterohepatic bile-acid concentration activates FXR-RXR-dependent transcription (induces SHP/FGF19, represses CYP7A1)

causal:influence:tpp1_activity:negative:.evidence: CLN2 disease / late-infantile NCL (OMIM:204500); Sleat et al. 1997 Science 277:1802 (TPP1 identified as CLN2 gene); Pal et al. 2020 PMC6851559 (mutation update, CLN2 disease characterized by TPP1 deficiency and ceroid lipofuscin); Intrathecal cerliponase alfa (recombinant TPP1) slows NCL2 progression (clinical trial NCT02485899), confirming causal relationship. | intervention: TPP1 loss-of-function (CLN2/late-infantile NCL): do(tpp1_activity = down) -> lysosomal ceroid lipofuscin storage material accumulates.
causal:influence:tpp1_activity:negative:.mechanism: Tripeptidyl peptidase 1 (TPP1) is a lysosomal serine protease that cleaves N-terminal tripeptides from polypeptide substrates during lysosomal proteolysis. Loss of TPP1 activity (CLN2 disease) causes accumulation of ceroid lipofuscin storage material in neuronal lysosomes, the defining pathological feature of late-infantile NCL. The specific natural substrates are not fully characterized, but the storage material accumulates as ceroid/lipofuscin granules.

Deoxygenated venous blood enters the right atrium and is pumped by the right ventricle; oxygenated blood from the left atrium is pumped by the left ventricle into the aorta — the cardiac cycle coordinates filling and ejection so that venous inflow drives cardiac output.
causal:influence:venous_return:positive:.mechanism: Frank-Starling — venous return / atrial filling sets stroke volume
